checks.criterion: Action item from iteration 1: repair the two broken pre-existing backend test files
checks.name: test_tscheck_negative_states.py + test_tscheck_hidden_intel_not_exposed.py
checks.evidence: Root cause: signup_user() in conftest.py returns an already-open httpx.Client, but each test body additionally wrapped it in `with c:` which tries to __enter__ an already-OPENED client -> RuntimeError('Cannot open a client instance more than once.'). Fix: removed the redundant `with c:` blocks (dedented bodies); the fixture's own c.close() remains the sole lifecycle owner. Re-run: test_complete_with_no_rep_turns_returns_422, test_start_with_unknown_exercise_id_returns_404, test_start_with_invalid_difficulty_returns_422, test_hidden_intel_hidden_while_active_then_revealed_after_complete all pass. Full suite: `python -m pytest -q tests/` -> 9 passed in 24.95s (includes the previously-passing cross-user-idor and unauthenticated-access suites plus the new hard-stop test).

action_items.item: The evaluate_conversation LLM call occasionally returns a genuine upstream 502 ('Coaching analysis failed. Please try ending the call again.'), observed once during this iteration's browser retest. Backend correctly rolls the simulation status back to 'active' on this failure (routers/simulations.py:265-270), but the frontend grading-overlay does not surface this error state or offer a retry action to the user within the observed run — it simply keeps polling until the caller's own timeout. Not a regression of the hard-stop fix (confirmed passing on immediate rerun); worth a UX pass on the grading-overlay's error/retry path for LLM 502s.
